findings.title: Missing merge-point/loop-header guard in FindContinuationForPolymorphicPropertyLoad
findings.message: In `FindContinuationForPolymorphicPropertyLoad`, after each `iterator_.Advance()` call the code immediately inspects the current bytecode without checking whether the new offset is a merge point or loop header. When the pattern `GetNamedProperty -> Star -> CallProperty` straddles a loop back-edge or a merge point, the iterator is advanced into that merge-point offset and a continuation is returned for it. Later, when Maglev tries to generate the polymorphic call inline graph and jump into the middle of what the graph considers a loop/merge block, the block's state machine is in an invalid state, triggering the DCHECK `state_ == kBlockPointer` in `maglev-ir.h`.
findings.suggestion: After each `iterator_.Advance()` call in `FindContinuationForPolymorphicPropertyLoad`, check whether the new offset is a merge point or loop header and return `{}` (no continuation) if so. Introduce a helper `IsOffsetAMergePointOrLoopHeader(int offset)` that combines `IsOffsetAMergePoint` and `bytecode_analysis().IsLoopHeader`.

ground_truth.root_cause: The function `FindContinuationForPolymorphicPropertyLoad` was introduced without the necessary guard that prevents it from identifying a continuation whose offsets land on bytecodes that are loop headers or merge points. Those offsets map to Maglev `MergePointInterpreterFrameState` objects that must be entered only via proper predecessor edges, not by jumping mid-continuation.
